code='''from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    # The full-color separator rows and columns divide the grid into panels.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    sep = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # In these puzzles the divider color spans complete rows and columns, while
    # the background is the most common remaining color.
    sep_rows = [r for r in range(h) if all(v == sep for v in grid[r])]
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h))]
    # If the divider is not the global mode (possible for unusually small grids),
    # detect full separator rows/columns directly.
    if not sep_rows:
        sep_rows = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
        sep_color = grid[sep_rows[0]][0] if sep_rows else None
    else:
        sep_color = sep
    if not sep_cols:
        sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    row_bounds = [-1] + sep_rows + [h]
    col_bounds = [-1] + sep_cols + [w]
    cells = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
             if r not in sep_rows and c not in sep_cols]
    background = Counter(cells).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for ra, rb in zip(row_bounds, row_bounds[1:]):
        line = []
        for ca, cb in zip(col_bounds, col_bounds[1:]):
            tile = [grid[r][c] for r in range(ra+1, rb) for c in range(ca+1, cb)]
            marker_count = sum(v != background for v in tile)
            line.append(1 if marker_count >= 2 else 3)
        out.append(line)
    return out
'''

path.write_text(code)
print(path, path.read_text())
